item.title: Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.30323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.
item.dc:creator: Jimin Choi, Max Z. Li

item.title: Computationally Transparent Power Flexibility Aggregation via Directional Support Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) creates new opportunities for improving resource adequacy, operational flexibility, and power-system reliability. However, efficiently characterizing the aggregate flexibility of heterogeneous DER portfolios remains challenging because of high dimensionality, diverse operating dynamics, and spatio-temporal coupling constraints. This paper proposes a computationally transparent framework that formulates aggregate flexibility characterization as a sequence of linear programming (LP)-based directional support evaluations. The framework accommodates heterogeneous DER technologies and configurable device-, feeder-, and portfolio-level constraints. The convex hull of the resulting boundary trajectories provides a feasible inner approximation of the coupled aggregate power flexibility region. Theoretical analysis establishes feasibility and non-overestimation guarantees and characterizes the computational dependence on portfolio size, scheduling horizon, and direction budget. In the small-scale case, the proposed method produces tighter projected regions than box, zonotope, and Chebyshev inner-ball benchmarks and matches a dense directional reference within numerical tolerance using 16--64 construction directions. Large-scale simulations with up to 2000 DERs demonstrate approximately linear empirical runtime scaling with the portfolio size and direction budget over the tested ranges. The results establish a scalable and theoretically grounded approach for aggregate DER flexibility characterization.
item.dc:creator: Mingyu Zhai, Liang Du, Yue Chen

item.title: Plug-in Estimation Method for Topology and Admittance Estimation in Electric Grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.30434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a scalable method for topology and admittance estimation in electric power grids. Our proposed plug-in estimation method incorporates precise phasor measurement unit data to estimate planned or unplanned grid topology and admittance parameter changes. Our plug-in estimation method decouples the problem into two stages: (i) constructing and averaging voltage coefficient matrices and current vectors from phasor data, and (ii) estimating admittance parameters via a least-squares regression approach with thresholding to recover the network topology. Rigidity matrix theory underpins the design of our plug-in estimation method --- to determine the data requirements (e.g., necessary and sufficient conditions) for accurate estimation of the grid topology and admittance parameters. By means of numerical simulations on the IEEE 13-node, 123-node, and European low voltage test feeders, we demonstrate the scalability of our plug-in estimation method and benchmark the computational time against a structured total least squares method. Our simulation results highlight the practicality of the proposed method for topology and admittance estimation in large-scale electric networks, including electric grids with partial topology information.
item.dc:creator: Norak Rin, Iman Shames, Ian R. Petersen, Nanduni I. Nimalsiri, Elizabeth L. Ratnam

item.title: Strategic Arbitrage in Electricity Markets: A Multi-Agent Policy Optimization Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.30446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grid-scale storage and load aggregators are growing quickly in wholesale electricity markets. If highly consolidated, these new participants may distort the competitive market equilibrium through strategic withholding behavior. Traditional market power mitigation techniques are ill-suited to arbitrage-based participants. We provide a multi-agent policy optimization model to study game-theoretic equilibria for real-time markets with consolidated storage and/or aggregators. The model is designed to facilitate natural first-order equilibrium-seeking update rules. We analyze the theoretical properties of different supply functions and their implications on the convergence of the gradient dynamics. Finally, we train equilibrium policies for a modified version of the IEEE RTS-GMLC benchmark across different levels of storage fleet consolidation, to demonstrate the potential of the framework as a tool to characterize and quantify strategic arbitrage.
item.dc:creator: Eli Brock, Srikar Babu Gadipudi, Somayeh Sojoudi, Javad Lavaei

item.title: LLM2Cert: LLM Synthesis of Certificates with SMT/Lean Verification
item.description: arXiv:2610.30524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates give state-space guarantees of stability and safety, but synthesizing and verifying them---especially for nonlinear, high-dimensional systems---remains an open challenge. Existing pipelines verify candidates with numerical solvers (sum-of-squares programs), interval methods, or satisfiability-modulo-theories (SMT) solvers, which often require relaxations, are conservative, or scale poorly with model dimension and nonlinearity. These limitations have also shaped benchmark design: standard test suites are dominated by low-dimensional polynomial systems chosen to suit what solvers can handle rather than what engineering applications require. We address both sides of this challenge. First, we introduce DynaCertBench, a benchmark of 105 instances: 80 non-redundant systems curated from the literature, extended with high-dimensional and control-constrained variants and new nonlinearly coupled systems, comprehensively spanning stability, region-of-attraction, forward-invariance, and safety tasks. Second, we present LLM2Cert, an LLM-driven framework that synthesizes candidate certificates and verifies them against their proof obligations: each obligation is routed to an SMT solver or directly to the Lean Proof-Repair agent. On DynaCertBench, LLM2Cert verifies 81 of 105 instances ($77.1\%$), a $17.1$ percentage point improvement over one-shot proposal without feedback. On the 81 fixed certificates, LLM2Cert verifies 22 that All-SMT leaves unresolved. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/llm2cert.
item.dc:creator: Zhipeng Cao, Peiyang Song, Nikolaus Vertovec, Weiru Cui, Zhihao Yang, Mingkang Liu, Luxia Lin, Bai Xue, Alessandro Abate

item.title: Using Finite-Time Control to Synthesize Dynamic Backup Control Barrier Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for the construction of control barrier functions (CBFs) for controllable linear systems subject to multiple state and input constraints. The approach is based on the Dynamic Backup CBF (DB-CBF) framework, where the control policy is parametrized using the equilibrium subspace of the system. By using a minimum-energy finite-time controller, we show that the terminal set constraint trivially reduces to having an admissible equilibrium point. The proposed DB-CBF is easy to tune (one parameter), fully takes advantage of the input range (by minimizing the control effort), and guarantees constraint enforcement (by tracking a backup equilibrium point that can be reached safely in finite time).
item.dc:creator: Victor Turpin-Aguayo, Victor Freire, Marco M. Nicotra

item.title: Exact Characterization of Admissible Bandwidths for Linear Disturbance Observers
item.description: arXiv:2610.30559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper characterizes the entire set of admissible Q-filter bandwidths, equivalently parameterized by the time constant $\tau$, that guarantee robust internal stability of a linear disturbance observer (DOB) under parametric plant uncertainties. Classical small-$\tau$ stability results provide a rigorous foundation for Q-filter bandwidth design. Building on this foundation, we formulate the $\tau$-dependent robust internal-stability problem as a semialgebraic feasibility problem in bivariate polynomials and prove that the complete admissible set is a finite union of open intervals under the standing assumptions. A constructive procedure with exact membership tests recovers all stabilizing intervals. A numerical example with an uncertain plant family containing non-minimum-phase members illustrates a disconnected admissible set.
item.dc:creator: Hamin Chang, Hyuntae Kim

item.title: Learning-Oriented Fault-Tolerant Control for UAVs with Time-Varying Fault Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in safety-critical applications has created a growing demand for control strategies that remain reliable in the presence of actuator and sensor faults. This paper presents a fault-tolerant control framework that combines constructive mathematical modeling, proportional--integral (PI) fault estimation, and learning-oriented control. A nonlinear quadcopter model is first developed using both the Newton--Euler and Euler--Lagrange formulations, from which a discrete-time linear model is derived for observer and controller design. A PI observer is then proposed to estimate actuator and sensor faults, with exponential estimation-error convergence established for constant faults in the absence of disturbances and ultimate boundedness established for slowly time-varying faults under bounded disturbances. The estimated fault signals are incorporated into an active fault-tolerant control architecture together with a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) controller, which is trained using only the yaw channel and subsequently applied to improve closed-loop tracking performance. Numerical simulations illustrate the observer's estimation performance under constant and slowly time-varying faults, including bounded disturbances, and the tracking performance of the integrated controller under multiple actuator and sensor fault scenarios. The proposed framework combines model-based fault estimation with learning-based control to improve fault accommodation and tracking performance in UAV systems.
item.dc:creator: Moh Kamalul Wafi

item.title: Half-Slot Link Scheduling for Open GNSS with $x$-Tx $y$-Rx Multibeam Phased Array Antennas
item.description: arXiv:2610.30695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSSs) are evolving from closed navigation constellations toward open space infrastructure capable of serving extensive spacecraft users. This evolution requires the constellation to support navigation ranging, telemetry (TM) return, and telecommand (TC) delivery for users while preserving its own ranging and communication functions.Existing phased-array payloads onboard BeiDou satellites provide one transmit (Tx) beam and one receive (Rx) beam. Such a configuration was designed mainly for intra-constellation operation, and can become a resource bottleneck when a large number of users share the same link opportunities. Upgrading GNSS satellites to phased-array terminals with $x$-Tx and $y$-Rx beams is therefore a natural enhancement. This paper develops a staged dynamic half-slot link scheduling framework (SDHSS) for open GNSS with $x$-Tx $y$-Rx multibeam phased-array antennas. The framework models navigation, TM, and TC as three different services, reserves the essential ranging and ground-access opportunities required by the GNSS constellation, and then allocates the remaining half-slot beam resources according to current service demand. To support multibeam concurrency, feasible links are selected through dynamic service-layer ordering and beam-copy matching. Simulations based on a BeiDou constellation show that the proposed method protects GNSS baseline operation and provides stronger external navigation, TM, and TC performance than fair contact planning. The results further show that additional Tx and Rx beams can be effectively converted into multi-service capability. This work establishes a link-scheduling approach for extending GNSS from constellation-internal operation to large-scale spacecraft service support.
item.dc:creator: Huan Yan, Kanglian Zhao, Wenfeng Li, Jinjun Zheng, Ziyu Wang, Changgang Zheng

item.title: Incentive Mechanisms for Welfare Maximization Under Individual Rationality in Noncooperative Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human societies are shaped by strategic interactions among self-interested decision-makers, where conflicts between individual and social interests naturally arise. This paper investigates the design of incentive mechanism for multi-agent game systems to reconcile social welfare maximization with individual benefits under economic constraints. We develop a linear-quadratic incentive framework to reshape Nash equilibria while reconciling the constraints of Pareto efficiency, individual rationality, and budget balance. The optimal target state is identified as the solution of a constrained optimization problem associated with the social welfare and aggregated payoff functions. Our theoretical analysis characterizes the conditions of incentive functions that steer self-interested agents towards the optimal target state as a Pareto-efficient Nash equilibrium for achieving the maximum attainable social welfare. We further characterize how the choice of social welfare function constrains achievable individual outcomes, revealing a structural paradox associated with priority weighting under individual rationality. Several numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the efficacy of our results.
item.dc:creator: Yuyue Yan, Maojiao Ye, Hideaki Ishii, Tomohisa Hayakawa

item.title: Anomaly Score Preserving Data Poisoning Attacks on Data-Driven Controller Design
item.description: arXiv:2610.30782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates stealthy data poisoning attacks against data-driven controller synthesis and develops an attack generation method. During data collection, an attacker can sequentially manipulate state measurements, while the defender attempts to detect such manipulation using a residual-based anomaly score based on the Mahalanobis distance. Under suitable assumptions on the defender's prior knowledge, we characterize the class of time-varying affine transformations that preserve the anomaly score for arbitrary data and parameterize this class by the orthogonal group. Based on this characterization, we formulate attack design under the stealthiness condition as an optimization problem over the orthogonal group and propose a Riemannian gradient method. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed attack can degrade closed-loop performance while remaining stealthy.
item.dc:creator: Motoharu Tsuboi, Hampei Sasahara, Iori Takaki, Hideaki Ishii

item.title: Consensus-Based Distributed Filtering for Angles-Only Tracking in Cislunar Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.30864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates consensus-based distributed filtering strategies for multi-observer angles-only navigation in the cislunar space. The objective is to estimate the inertial state of a target spacecraft using only line-of-sight measurements collected by a network of observer spacecraft. This problem is particularly relevant for autonomous cislunar navigation, where ground support may be limited, and centralized fusion architectures may be problematic due to communication and computational constraints, and single-point failure risks. Three distributed filtering approaches are considered: the Distributed Extended Kalman Filter, the Information-Weighted Consensus Filter, and the Kalman Consensus Filter. All methods share the same local prediction and measurement-processing steps, but differ in the way information is exchanged and fused across the network. Their performance is evaluated and compared to a centralized Extended Kalman Filter, adopted as benchmark, and independent local filters in a high-fidelity cislunar scenario. Numerical simulations show that the distributed approaches significantly improve estimation accuracy with respect to independent filters. Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses are then conducted to characterize the robustness of the considered methods to finite consensus iterations and prior misalignment among the agents.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Romagnoli, Fabrizio Pilone, Giordana Bucchioni

item.title: Archive coverage constrains abstaining retrieval for transient stability screening more than conditional accuracy
item.description: arXiv:2610.30996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power-grid transient stability is assessed by simulating credible faults, but repeating simulations as operating conditions change is costly, motivating faster critical clearing time estimators. Within the AI-ASSIST project, we developed a retrieval-based estimator around three adopted requirements: estimates retain their supporting states, retrieval abstains without compatible support, and support statistics are tested against observed error. Abstention turns estimator uncertainty into a demand on the archive. Exact switching-configuration equality is used. The dense synthetic BUS39 archive covers 99.9996% of 1,044,797 records; the operational ELES archive covers 73.47% of 322,823 records. At query time, 59.37% of ELES states have an earlier same-topology candidate. Under causal availability, retrieval covers 56.34% of records; on records covered under both protocols, mean absolute error increases by 10.0%. No tested support diagnostic ranks first on both grids. Most tested supervised regressors have lower error than retrieval on BUS39, all higher on the matched retrieval-covered ELES population. On ELES, gradient boosting becomes more accurate than retrieval when temporally adjacent states are excluded, so the accuracy trade depends on the archive. Under the adopted compatibility key, archive availability constrains deployment more than conditional accuracy on ELES. Compatible coverage and chronological availability are auditable before an estimator is fitted.
item.dc:creator: Gregor Cerar, Denis Sodin, Matja\v{z} \v{S}krlec, Urban Rude\v{z}, Mihael Mohor\v{c}i\v{c}, Miha Smolnikar

item.title: Stability-Preserving Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneity-Aware Composite Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.31037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) provides a flexible mechanism for adapting traffic signal control to heterogeneous traffic and sensing conditions, but directly learned signal actions do not automatically inherit the analytical properties of structured traffic-control methods. This paper proposes Com-MP, a theory-guided RL framework that learns a context-dependent composition of multiple max-pressure (MP) control preferences while retaining decentralized MP phase selection. The learned policy adapts the relative influence of constituent MP formulations according to local traffic and sensing conditions, allowing data-driven adaptation to operate within a structured traffic-control framework. We show that such intersection-specific and time-varying composition preserves strong queue stability for every demand in the strictly stabilizable region under any admissible non-anticipative composition policy, thereby separating the performance-adaptation role of learning from the stability property of the underlying controller. In a representative implementation combining detector-supported queue-based MP and connected-vehicle-supported travel-time MP, experiments on a real-world 45-intersection network show that Com-MP reduces average delay by 15.6\% and 8.6\% relative to the two constituent controllers, respectively, and by about 7.0\% relative to the best fixed composition. The learned composition responds systematically to local traffic and sensing conditions, remains effective under heterogeneous and degraded sensing, and can be transferred without retraining to an unseen network with an average delay only 2.4\% higher than that of a policy trained directly on the target network. These results show how learning-based adaptation can be introduced within a stability-preserving traffic-control structure, providing a theory-guided pathway toward trustworthy learning-enabled traffic signal control.
item.dc:creator: Jichen Zhu, Chaopeng Tan

item.title: Cross-Region Cooperation of UAV Swarms Towards Air-Ground ISAC via Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.31054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The limited communication resources and sensing perspectives of a single uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) motivate UAV swarms for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in air-ground networks. However, in multi-region scenarios, regional UAV allocations may not match vehicle demand, while local observations may lack sufficient diversity for accurate sensing. To address these issues, this paper proposes a cross-region cooperation framework for UAV swarms. For communication, cross-region UAV reallocation reduces service disparities by matching resources to vehicle demand. For sensing, combining UAV observations from different regions increases observation diversity, while adaptive handshaking guided by marginal Cram\'er--Rao bound (CRB) utilities balances phase synchronization gains against handshaking energy consumption. Joint optimization of UAV positions and transmit power within each region then further improves communication service and sensing performance. These coupled decisions are coordinated by a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (H-MARL) approach through slow-timescale inter-region UAV reallocation and fast-timescale intra-region UAV control. Under the considered simulation settings, reallocation can improve quality of service (QoS) by over 20 percentage points compared with retaining the initial allocation under severe resource-demand mismatches. Cooperative sensing with adaptive handshaking incurs only about a 5.0% increase in mean CRB relative to perfect synchronization.
item.dc:creator: Linghui Miao, Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Shijian Gao

item.title: Large Language Models Meet Bayesian Optimization: Towards Self-evolving Wireless Digital Twins
item.description: arXiv:2610.31192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wireless digital twins (DTs) are increasingly integrated with artificial intelligence to support online modeling, prediction, and network optimization. However, most existing approaches perform adaptation within predefined learning or optimization structures, which may become unsuitable when wireless tasks and operating conditions change. In this article, we investigate the integration of large language models (LLMs) and Bayesian optimization (BO) to extend wireless DTs from online adaptation towards algorithm-level self-evolution. We introduce an LLM-assisted BO framework in which BO provides a stable and sample-efficient optimization backbone, while the LLM determines whether selected BO components should be retained or adapted based on the current task and accumulated optimization experience. In simulations, we apply the framework to Gaussian process (GP) kernel discovery for a multi-user wireless beam-selection problem. Simulation results show that the LLM-discovered kernel improves the final BO performance by 19.7% on the training tasks compared with the strongest standard kernel baseline. The results demonstrate the potential of combining LLM flexibility with structured BO for self-evolving wireless DTs.
item.dc:creator: Yingzhuo Sun, Haoyun Li, Ming Xiao, Francisco J. Ferrao, Berna Ozbek

item.title: Constrained Sparsest Input Selection for Structural Controllability is NP-Hard
item.description: arXiv:2610.31195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of selecting the fewest admissible input--state links that make a structured linear system structurally controllable. This objective counts nonzero entries from prescribed positions of the input matrix and is different from minimizing its number of nonzero columns. Prior work gives polynomial-time algorithms for several restricted cases, including single or dedicated inputs and prescribed input patterns satisfying additional graph-theoretic conditions. We give a polynomial-time reduction from perfect three-dimensional matching, establishing for the first time that the decision problem is NP-complete and the optimization problem is NP-hard. A refinement of the reduction yields an exact optimum relation and shows that the problem is APX-hard. An example also exhibits a strict integrality gap for the natural linear programming relaxation.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Zhang, Jintao Zhang, Yun Feng

item.title: Feeder-Aware Service-Conditioned Flexibility of Grid-Interactive Buildings
item.description: arXiv:2610.31204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grid-interactive buildings can adjust demand, but building-feasible power budgets may differ from accepted feeder-head offers. This study addresses a practical question: to what extent can the adjustable electricity consumption of buildings be translated into deliverable flexibility services while satisfying feeder-head operating requirements? To enable a fair comparison, we adopt the same baseline operating schedule, equipment conditions, and post-service recovery requirements for indoor temperature and battery state of charge (SOC). Flexibility is then evaluated under two settings: one considering only building-level constraints, and the other additionally accounting for feeder-head constraints. We first use a simplified network model with explicit security margins to determine a preliminary amount of flexibility that can be committed. The resulting schedule is then validated using a more detailed network simulation via Modelica. If network losses cause the actual response to deviate from the committed response, the electricity consumption of individual buildings is rescheduled. If the required response still cannot be achieved, the committed flexibility level is reduced. The experiments cover multiple service activation times, regulation directions, and service durations. For comparative purposes, we retain the initial optimization result as the reference estimate of the maximum potentially available flexibility, rather than interpreting the failure of a particular subsequent realization attempt as evidence that a larger flexibility level is inherently infeasible. The results demonstrated that 24.51\% of nonzero flexibility contracts were rejected due to feeder-head constraints, 67.04\% of contracts were accepted with some rescheduling and building redispatch, and only 8.09\% of contracts were accepted without any changes.
item.dc:creator: Dafang Zhao, Ittetsu Taniguchi, Takao Onoye

item.title: Model Predictive Control of Wind Turbines: A Model-Oriented Review of Prediction Models, Control Objectives, and Nonlinear Aerodynamic Formulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.31295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has been applied to wind-turbine regulation with markedly different internal prediction models, ranging from linearized low-order turbine models to nonlinear, aeroelastic, floating, and data-driven predictors. This review organizes the literature primarily by the model propagated by the controller and treats model order, predictor representation, MPC formulation, control objective, and validation plant as separate descriptors. Primary studies show that low-order linear or piecewise-affine predictors are attractive for constrained power and speed regulation, whereas flexible drivetrain, structural, and floating models are needed when drivetrain twist, tower motion, blade loads, or platform dynamics are explicit control quantities. Nonlinear and economic MPC studies further demonstrate coordinated pitch/torque control across broad operating regions, while preview, repetitive, and data-driven formulations address wind prediction, periodic loads, and model mismatch. Particular attention is given to aerodynamic pitch dependence: variable-pitch turbine dynamics can be non-affine with respect to applied pitch, and the term NMPC alone does not prove that the original nonlinear pitch map is retained inside the optimizer. The review therefore adopts a conservative, equation-based classification for direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation. Here, direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation means that the applied pitch at each prediction step is evaluated inside the original nonlinear aerodynamic map, rather than replacing that dependence by a linearized, scheduled, piecewise-affine, or learned surrogate. The literature supports a remaining integration challenge at the intersection of flexible drivetrain prediction, nonlinear aerodynamic pitch treatment, explicit constraints and load objectives, and validated adaptive or learned model correction.
item.dc:creator: Roya Khalili-Amirabadi, Mohsen Jalaeian-Farimani, Mahdi Ghane

item.title: Transfer Meta-Learning for State Space Autoencoders
item.description: arXiv:2610.31318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear system identification often requires costly experimental campaigns and separate model fitting for each different instance (target system) of a given system family. To reduce this burden, meta-learning approaches reuse information acquired across related systems. In particular, in-context meta-learning enables zero-shot prediction from a brief target system context (i.e., a short input-output trajectory), but generally yields large black-box sequence predictors without exposing an explicit state space model. Conversely, compact structured state space models are suitable for simulation, estimation, and control, but are usually fitted or adapted separately for each target system. To bridge this gap, we introduce a transfer meta-learning extension of state space autoencoders. The method reuses a pretrained encoder, whose weights remain fixed, to extract a compact representation of the target system from its context. An affine parameterization maps this representation to the parameters of a compact neural state space model without target-specific adaptation; the resulting model contains orders of magnitude fewer parameters than the reference in-context predictors from the literature. We evaluate zero-shot prediction and simulation performance on held-out system instances from Buck-Boost converter and Bouc-Wen oscillator system families, comparing performance against individually fitted baseline models.
item.dc:creator: Stefano De Carli, Daniele Masti, Davide Previtali, Mirko Mazzoleni

item.title: Barrier Function Control for the Interconnection of DC Electronic Loads to Utility Grid
item.description: arXiv:2610.31488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a nonlinear control law that facilitates the safe integration of DC electronic loads to the utility grid. Specifically, by employing suitable reciprocal barrier functions, it is rigorously proven that the closed-loop system guarantees constrained operation within a desired operating region, despite the influence of fast converter dynamics and fluctuating constant power load demand. This way, the proposed controller guarantees safety of the electronic components from surges in power demand and high transients. The theoretic results are validated in simulation scenarios, where the performance of the proposed controller is compared against the conventional saturated-PI controller. Contrary to the latter, the proposed method guarantees stable and safe operation, enhancing the system robustness.
item.dc:creator: Grigoris Michos, Christos K. Verginis

item.title: History-Aware Control Barrier Functionals with Nonsingular Fading-Memory Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.31525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety-critical protection often depends not only on the state and physical limits of the system, but on how that state evolved over time. Here, the safety margin measures the remaining allowance before a physical limit is reached. In this context, the objective is to enforce both physical safety and history-dependent retention of this margin for integer-order control-affine systems. To this end, changes in this margin are converted into memory through fading-memory kernels with finite nonnegative weights. A history-aware control barrier functional (HA-CBFal) is constructed explicitly, with nonnegativity equivalent to retaining a prescribed fraction of this margin's weighted historical value. This condition is enforced by an affine input constraint and proved to imply physical safety under stated kernel, initialization, and feasibility conditions, without finite-dimensional memory realization. In 36 calibration cases on the ADMIRE flight-control benchmark, mean per-case tracking-RMSE reductions of 27.2\% and 7.0\% are obtained relative to calibrated state-only CBF and moving-average control barrier functional (MA-CBFal), respectively, with both constraints preserved to numerical tolerance. In a shorter-recovery maneuver outside calibration with frozen gains, both constraints are preserved to tolerance by HA-CBFal and state-only CBF, but the retention requirement is violated despite MA-CBFal nonnegativity.
item.dc:creator: Ege C. Altunkaya, Esra Demir, Murad Abu-Khalaf, \.Ibrahim \"Ozkol

item.title: Space Solar Applications: Simulation with MATLAB-Simulink Environment and Transmission of Solar Power Generated
item.description: arXiv:2610.31542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper a photovoltaic (PV) array suitable for use in outer space is simulated in the MATLAB/Simulink environment. The simulation of the PV array is first carried out with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and then without MPPT. In a second step, the response of the system to different irradiation levels is observed. A brief overview of the transmission of solar power generated in space down to the earth via microwaves is also given. Selected simulation results are provided for a comparative study of both cases.
item.dc:creator: Ferhat S. Demirci, Murari Koushik Muthu Kannapiran

item.title: Decentralized Bi-Level Optimization for Cooperative Orbital Transportation of a Rigid Payload
item.description: arXiv:2610.31562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of the space economy, alongside increasing orbital congestion and debris, is driving demand for reliable on-orbit transportation of large and non-cooperative objects. Performing such transportation with a swarm of small spacecraft distributes risk and removes the single point of failure inherent to monolithic architectures, but requires solving a non-convex trajectory optimization coupling every agent's cone-constrained thrust to the payload's rotational dynamics. Existing approaches span decentralized control laws with asymptotic guarantees but limited constraint enforcement, and centralized and partially centralized planners that reintroduce a single point of failure. In this work, we present a decentralized bi-level framework driven by exact gradients: the problem is split into an inner convex thrust allocation and an outer search over payload torque trajectories. This decomposition yields fuel-efficient solutions quickly, without requiring full NLP convergence, and at short timescales its performance scales with the number of agents. Theoretical convergence guarantees are established, and the method is validated through extensive Monte Carlo simulation, including closed-loop recovery from in-flight faults. These properties make the framework well suited to spacecraft swarm applications.
item.dc:creator: Sidhdharth D. Sikka, Revathy Ravuri, Hei Yin Jowett Chan, Tim Echtermeyer, Shaoshuai Mou

item.title: The EU AI Act Beyond Europe: A Practical Readiness Framework for Non-EU Organisations. Comparative Evidence from Four African Countries
item.description: arXiv:2610.30152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act has implications for organizations within Europe as well as organisations outside the European Union where they provide AI-enabled services to EU clients, use European vendors, participate in EU-facing supply chains, or generate outputs that are used in the EU. This study examines the implications of these impacts for African countries and other non-EU organisations, using South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya and Egypt as comparative cases. It applies doctrinal legal analysis, structured document review and scenario-based comparison to assess the sufficiency or otherwise of existing regulatory frameworks within the selected countries. The analysis shows that the existing regulatory frameworks (like data-protection, financial-sector, cybersecurity and corporate-governance rules) can support AI readiness, but they do not resolve questions of territorial scope, role classification, risk categorisation, vendor responsibility and access to compliance evidence. The analysis proposes a seven-step readiness framework which covers exposure mapping, AI inventories, role and risk classification, governance, contracts, evidence management and continuous monitoring. It argues for proportionate, interoperable approaches that enable non-EU organisations to demonstrate readiness without treating EU compliance as a uniform exercise.
item.dc:creator: Uloma Okoro, Branislav Radeljic

item.title: On the Adversarial Vulnerability of Neural Receivers with Unrolled LDPC Decoders
item.description: arXiv:2610.30345v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural receivers for 5G New Radio (NR) match classical model-based receivers in link-level performance, but their robustness to adversarial perturbations at the receiver input remains underexplored. We show that standard gradient-based attacks applied end-to-end through an unrolled low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoder fail to significantly outperform a matched-power Gaussian perturbation. We identify the failure as gradient masking caused by tanh saturation in the boxplus operation of the belief-propagation (BP) check-node update, with a per-iteration gradient norm decay of more than four orders of magnitude across ten unrolled BP iterations. Based on this finding, we propose two structurally independent loss functions that restore attack efficacy. L_BP routes the gradient through the unsaturated early iterations via per-iteration supervision, while L_LLR is a margin loss on pre-decoder log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) whose gradient bypasses the LDPC decoder entirely. Both loss functions increase the block-error rate (BLER) by one to four orders of magnitude at matched perturbation power, with the results reproduced on both the Sionna NeuralReceiver and DeepRx. At low PSR, L_LLR-optimized perturbations achieve up to three orders of magnitude higher BLER on unseen channel realizations than LBP-optimized perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Aakash Saini, Jafar Aco Mohammadi, Wolfgang Gerstacker

item.title: Integrated Longitudinal and Lateral Control for High-Speed Platooning of Articulated Vehicles
item.description: arXiv:2610.30437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents an integrated control framework for high-speed platooning of articulated vehicles, combining advanced longitudinal and lateral control strategies to address the challenges of safe and efficient autonomous driving. A novel proof of string stability for the proposed longitudinal control algorithm, based on a PID framework, ensures robust inter-vehicle distance regulation even under dynamic operating conditions. Additionally, an arc-length-based longitudinal error formulation enhances the applicability of the control system for curved roads, making it realistic for diverse driving scenarios. For lateral control, significant improvements to the clothoid-based path tracking algorithm are introduced to mitigate oscillations and enhance stability at high speeds. These enhancements include a tangential criterion for oscillation reduction, trajectory segment classification for adaptive lookahead distance tuning, a dual-adaptive mechanism for regulating the rate of lookahead distance adjustments based on both cross-track error (CTE) and anticipated road curvature, and extensions for articulated vehicle dynamics. The proposed integrated control framework is validated through simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in maintaining stability, minimizing tracking errors, and ensuring robust performance in high-speed and challenging platooning scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Aashish Shaju, Steve Southward, Mehdi Ahmadian

item.title: Learning to Incentivise: Using Reinforcement Learning for Sustainable Urban Mobility
item.description: arXiv:2610.30469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Traffic management has traditionally focused on toll-based and road pricing solutions. However, road pricing often raises concerns about accessibility and public dissatisfaction, leading to its prohibition in some places, such as Finland. This study optimises the dynamic allocation of incentives to drivers, encouraging them to reroute onto alternative (potentially longer) paths to achieve greater societal benefit, reduced total travel time (TTT) and total emissions in the transportation network, contributing to sustainable urban mobility. We employ a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach to dynamically assign incentives to drivers to reduce both TTT and emissions, with travel times estimated using traffic simulation software. We demonstrate that, with an unlimited budget and an objective of minimising travel time, the incentive scheme reduces TTT by 16%, compared to the dynamic User-Equilibrium (UE) with a budget equivalent to about 11% of the UE total time. When the goal is to minimise emissions, a 9% reduction in CO2 emissions is observed under an unlimited budget. We demonstrate a critical trade-off: minimising TTT leads to an increase in emissions, while prioritising emission reductions raises TTT. However, with the right combination of weights in the multi-objective function, both TTT and total emissions are improved beyond the baseline.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 2025 9th International Conference on Models and Technologies for Intelligent Transportation Systems (MT-ITS), IEEE, 2025
item.dc:creator: Germ\'an Pardo-Gonz\'alez, Shaghayegh Vosough, Katerina Papadaki, Claudio Roncoli

item.title: On the Structure of Quantum Finite-Level Systems: Decoherence-Free Subsystems, Quantum Nondemolition Variables, and Back-Action-Evading Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.30616v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to conduct a comprehensive structural analysis of quantum finite-level systems in the Heisenberg picture, where the evolution of system observables is modeled by bilinear quantum stochastic differential equations (QSDEs). Firstly, real coordinate transformations that preserve commutation and anticommutation relations are characterized, and relative admissibility between different orthonormal Hermitian bases is formulated. Secondly, strongly aligned subspaces are introduced, based on which decoherence-free subsystems (DFSs) are constructed in general orthonormal Hermitian basis as well as the generalized Gell-Mann basis. Thirdly, conditions for the existence of quantum nondemolition (QND) variables are given in terms of both linear systems theory and spectral separation by output-signal observables. Finally, a sufficient condition for quantum back-action-evading (BAE) measurements is established. A four-qubit nearest-neighbor Heisenberg chain with collective dephasing illustrates these structural properties of quantum finite-level systems.
item.dc:creator: Jia Gu, Guofeng Zhang, Ian R. Petersen

item.title: Behavioral Mapping of Hierarchical Dynamical Models Accelerates Bayesian Parameter Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.30683v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayesian parameter inference for complex nonlinear dynamical models is often limited by the cost of repeated model simulation. We present a behavioral mapping framework that uses the inferred posterior of a higher-level model to accelerate inference of a lower-level model without requiring state or parameter correspondence between them. Building on approximate simulation relations for hierarchically related models, we define the notion of behavioral compatibility and quantify the behavioral support of detailed model parameters using the reduced model posterior. We learn a level set of behavioral support using a Gaussian process and use it to filter detailed model parameter proposals before expensive simulations during Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) inference. We derive conditions under which the behavioral support level set retains all detailed model parameters that fit the experimental data within a prescribed tolerance. We apply this method to a hierarchy of gene-expression models fitted to cell-free experimental data. After initial setup costs, our approach speeds up MCMC by 8.02% for the phenomenological model and 15.21% for the mechanistic model.
item.dc:creator: Jingsong Bai, Ayush Pandey

item.title: Numerical Solution of Large-Scale Low-Rank Coupled Generalized Sylvester Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.30804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper develops projection methods for computing low-rank solutions to large-scale coupled generalized Sylvester equations. The dominant subspaces of these solutions are shown to be spanned by specific resolvent directions, motivating a Petrov--Galerkin projection framework. Conditions for the unique solvability of the projected coupled generalized Sylvester equations are also discussed. Based on these dominant subspaces, two algorithms are proposed: an extended Krylov-based projection algorithm and a rational Krylov-based projection algorithm. The former uses fixed shifts, whereas the latter uses adaptive shifts. Numerical experiments on large-scale benchmark problems demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve high accuracy and fast convergence.
item.dc:creator: Umair Zulfiqar

item.title: PriMa-Causa: Causal Prescriptive Maintenance
item.description: arXiv:2610.31147v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated manufacturing requires data-driven decisions under uncertainty and sparse observational records, and unplanned downtime is a dominant cost of getting them wrong. Prescriptive maintenance recommends a maintenance action against an impending failure rather than merely predicting it. Established reference architectures couple predictive models with rule- or optimisation-based recommendation logic. Selecting a corrective action, however, requires an interventional quantity: how the line behaviour would change if the action were set. Manufacturing data is observational, so a model fitted to predict the outcome estimates an associational quantity and may misdirect the choice of action without the prediction error revealing it. Causal estimators target the interventional quantity but require an expert-led causal study per case, for which the bounded decision window of operation leaves no room. This dissertation analyses how causal reasoning can be embedded into prescriptive maintenance so that actions are ranked by their estimated interventional effect. The result is PriMa-Causa, built from three components: a causal reasoning layer that integrates the estimate into the PriMa reference model, a parametric simulator that supplies the interventional ground truth absent from manufacturing data, and a graph-conditioned tabular causal foundation model that, pre-trained once on this synthetic production-line prior, answers interventional queries in a single forward pass. PriMa-Causa attains a lower prescription error than associational baselines, with the largest margin under weak overlap and sparse context, and a partially disclosed causal graph reduces this error further. The causal inductive bias of the synthetic prior and the graph conditioning can thus replace per-case estimator fitting, a step toward automating causal inference for autonomous and self-healing maintenance.
item.dc:creator: Felix Saretzky

item.title: Calibration-free IMU-based Relative Orientation Estimation under Dynamic Human Motion
item.description: arXiv:2610.31156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent magnetometer-free inertial measurement unit (IMU) methods can reduce drift in joint motion estimation using rigid-body constraints, but they typically require pre-calibrated sensor locations, assumptions of specific joint models (e.g., hinge joints) or limited motion types, or an external reference for global orientation. Furthermore, challenges related to high-frequency impacts (e.g. at foot strikes during gait) and numerical differentiation of noisy measurements have not been explicitly addressed. We propose an extended Kalman filter that estimates relative IMU orientation and sensor location simultaneously, requiring neither offline sensor location calibration nor a global orientation anchor. A systematic simulation study shows that the quality of the relative orientation and the sensor location estimates depends on different motion-intensity sources: the joint center acceleration and the relative angular velocity, respectively. A low-pass filter (LPF) is used to mitigate real-signal outliers before applying the rigid-body constraint. When applied to the OpenSense dataset with real IMU measurements across four subjects with three lower-body joint types during walking and complex tasks including various motion types, the proposed method achieves an overall relative orientation error of 2.61{\deg}, compared with 10.40{\deg} for a baseline using offline-estimated sensor locations and 7.43{\deg} for a baseline using marker-derived sensor locations. These results show that the proposed calibration-free estimation framework handles real IMU data effectively and achieves accurate relative orientation without offline sensor location calibration.
item.dc:creator: Ruiyuan Li, Hassan Osman, Ajay Seth, Manon Kok

item.title: Evolving Federated Density Peak Clustering with Shuffler-Based Anonymization
item.description: arXiv:2610.31211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we present a novel one-shot federated clustering approach based on evolving fuzzy clustering and shuffler-based anonymization. In federated clustering, each round reveals additional model information to the server and can increase the opportunity to infer properties of local datasets, even when raw samples are never shared. Consequently, fewer client-server exchanges and unlinkability are important, so transmitted information cannot be attributed to any single client. Data-stream clustering algorithms, which learn in a single pass over the data, align well with the one-shot federated learning paradigm, where a single communication round can be sufficient. The proposed Evolving Federated Density Peak Clustering (eFDPC) method combines evolving fuzzy data-stream clustering and density peak clustering in a federated setting. Each client independently evolves micro-clusters from private data mini-batches through cluster addition and merging. To limit communication, density peak clustering is applied to the learned micro-clusters and only the selected peaks are transmitted, rather than the full local models. A shuffler-based layer is introduced between the clients and the server to anonymize contributions prior to reconstruction and global peak selection. We consider a peak-only variant, eFDPC-P, as well as eFDPC-G with server-side label propagation. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmark datasets show that eFDPC outperforms recent federated clustering baselines in one-shot settings and scales to higher-dimensional, non-IID data.
item.dc:creator: Miha O\v{z}bot, Seiichi Ozawa, Igor \v{S}krjanc

item.title: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action
item.description: arXiv:2610.31376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies the problem of safe tool execution for large language model (LLM) agents under prompt injection. Using Petri nets, we formalize the execution harness between the LLM and its tools as a supervisory control problem, in which marks represent capabilities, approvals and budgets. Since a transition fires only if the marks it needs are present, an injected request whose preconditions are unmet or already spent is refused regardless of its wording. Treating tool outcomes as uncontrollable, we enforce safety by the conventional maximally permissive supervisor, and this safety transfers to the running system under four assumptions. Moreover, to capture an agent that may propose again after a refusal, we introduce the notion of a replanning closed loop, in which each retry costs an inference call. We show that, in this loop, the conventional supervisor can be arbitrarily more intrusive than a stricter safe one. Furthermore, for a given proposer model, the maximally permissive least-intrusive supervisor is characterized as a value-threshold refinement of the conventional one. Under precise conditions, this refinement orders two concurrent actions by at most one monitor place. On an autonomous release agent, we find by synthesis that safe deployment requires a step that the supervisor can refuse after a rollout starts.
item.dc:creator: Chao Gu, Quanyan Zhu

item.title: Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona)
item.description: arXiv:2610.31526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training. By casting the values and derivatives at the query and neighbouring samples as latent variables in a constrained optimisation problem, the burden of long training loops becomes one of on-demand local solves. We establish Diona's theoretical properties including finite-sample coverage and, in the noiseless case, convergence to the true state and derivatives under dense sampling. In a nonlinear regression benchmark on six functions of three to eight dimensions, Diona was more accurate than a Gaussian process (GP) on noiseless data especially with denser data sets. Furthermore, as with GP, it produced uncertainty bounds that contained the true value at more than 95% of query points in four functions. Diona's time to a first prediction after a data set update was three to four orders of magnitude shorter than that of the GP, and two to three orders shorter than that of a neural network, which was more accurate but offers no uncertainty quantification. This low latency is paid for by on-demand predictions, so this latency advantage applies when relatively few predictions are needed between data updates.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Sabug Jr., Eric Kerrigan

item.title: Controlled Radio Fault Injection and Telemetry Evaluation for Open 5G RANs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radio access network (RAN) telemetry reveals radio conditions, protocol behavior, and their consequences for applications. Evaluating its usefulness requires controlled impairments and observations of the same execution. We present C and Python channel brokers and a fault injection workflow for software 5G testbeds connecting an OCUDU base station and a software UE through ZeroMQ. The brokers apply scheduled, directional transformations to I/Q samples and restore the link, while the workflow jointly records applied faults, native and programmable (codelet) telemetry, and application delay. We demonstrate this capability through 45 comparative trials of brief uplink interruptions and stepped additive noise. These use cases distinguish recognizing a radio change from measuring its service consequence: native missing-feedback events retrospectively identify interruptions, whereas noise changes decoding-error measurements without producing those events. Median on-time round-trip times remain near 30 ms, but the prespecified comparisons show mean increases in on-time 95th-percentile delay of 354 and 604 ms for one and five interruptions, and 113 ms for noise. Adding receive-side radio link control (RLC) codelet summaries did not improve interruption classification on held-out trials. The framework provides a reusable way to evaluate measurement choices under known radio faults, before using them in monitoring or learning systems.
item.dc:creator: Babak Azkaei, Maxim B\^itiu, Georgios Exarchakos, Kishor Chandra Joshi

item.title: Extending Harmonic Function Methods via Root Locus for Coordinated Path Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.31625v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the offline generation of coordinated paths for N interchangeable robots and N goals in planar environments with polygonal obstacles. After a conformal map to a circular domain, starts and goals become the poles and zeros of a rational function R, and the paths are the branches of its Generalized Root Locus (GRL), i.e. the streamlines of the logarithmic potential -log R. We show that, for every phase outside a finite set of critical phases and a set of boundary phases, the induced gradient motion drives each robot to a distinct goal along pairwise disjoint paths that never reach the obstacles; the robot-goal assignment is produced by the construction, and with the gain used as a clock all robots move as the closed-loop roots of the GRL and arrive together at a prescribed time. Obstacles become streamlines through successive Milne-Thomson reflections, and for a finite number of reflections a finite test certifies safety for the potential that is actually computed. Reciprocal root-locus planning is recovered as a special case. The method is illustrated on two polygonal workspaces, 100 random instances compared with independent harmonic planning and artificial potentials, and a scene with ten robots and ten obstacles.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Frascarelli, Lucia Pallottino, Alberto Landi

item.title: Workload-Aware Monitoring for AI-RAN
item.description: arXiv:2610.31627v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-RAN platforms are expected to share CPU and GPU resources between radio workloads and AI services. Aggregate telemetry reports operating conditions, but timing changes may reflect different workloads, processors, or measurement boundaries. We propose workload-aware monitoring that associates radio-work descriptors with processing paths, timing boundaries, and operating context before comparing like with like. In 16 over-the-air downlink experiments, hybrid dispatch (CPU for transport blocks (TBs) below 4,096 bytes and GPU otherwise) has 29.66% and 22.93% lower mean host-callback durations than direct GPU dispatch, without and with a synthetic GPU co-runner, respectively. Grouping locates the separation in small TBs, while large-TB callback-duration ranges overlap. These observations identify a candidate for complementary CPU/GPU use.
item.dc:creator: Babak Azkaei, Georgios Exarchakos, Kishor Chandra Joshi

item.title: OpenTac: An Open Ecosystem for Customizable, Scalable, and Transferable 3D Tactile Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2610.31661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present OpenTac, a novel sensor and a full-stack ecosystem for tactile skins that are highly customizable, scalable, and readily deployed in downstream robot control and learning applications. Our core contribution is twofold. First, we develop a scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure. Differential responses across neighboring "taxels" support decoding of local shear vectors, and the common-mode response encodes normal force. Second, we provide a highly customizable sensor design tool that is able to automatically generate fabrication files for these tactile skins from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, including from abstract descriptions such as text (e.g., "design a sensor for a size 9 shoe insole"). We develop an ecosystem around the OpenTac sensor, including the CAD design tool, a sensor simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and fast/adaptive data acquisition. We demonstrate the broad applicability of the OpenTac-CAD sensor design tool by designing and fabricating more than 30 sensors across a variety of robot embodiments. We characterize the three-dimensional tactile fields produced by OpenTac with a commercial, high-precision force/torque sensor. We demonstrate the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments. Additionally, adaptive acquisition enables kilohertz-rate partial readouts, exceeding full-array raster scanning on the same sensor by 19.2X at 16 sampled taxels per update for a 1024-taxel skin. We provide all hardware, software, and result videos are at opentac.github.io
item.dc:creator: Ariel Slepyan, Geeta Chandra Raju Bethala, Jiafeng Gu, Anagha Rajendra Dangle, Yinzhe Zhou, Hongyuan Fu, Jade Sim, Tuhin Basu, Xinyi Yin, Md Faizal Karim, Gregory Hager, Homanga Bharadhwaj, Anand Bhattad, Krishna Murthy Jatavallabhula, Nitish V. Thakor

item.title: Opinion Dynamics in Social Multiplex Networks with Mono and Bi-directional Interactions in the Presence of Leaders
item.description: arXiv:2401.15857v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We delve into the dynamics of opinions within a multiplex network using coordination games, where agents communicate either through one-way or two-way interactions, and where a designated leader may be present. By employing graph theory and Markov chains, we illustrate that despite zero diagonal elements in transition probability matrices or decomposable layers, opinions converge under specific conditions on the layers, leading to a consensus, and we show by a counterexample that a spanning tree in the union of the layers does not suffice. We further scrutinize the convergence rates of opinion dynamics in networks with one-way versus two-way interactions. We find that in networks with a designated leader, opinions converge towards the initial opinion of the leader, whereas in networks without a designated leader, opinions converge to a convex combination of the opinions of agents. Moreover, we emphasize the crucial role of designated leaders in steering opinion convergence within the network. Paired experiments on 1,200 random multiplex networks show that a leader slows down convergence, and that two-way interactions slow it down in the presence of a leader but speed it up in its absence.
item.dc:creator: Amirreza Talebi, Sayed Pedram Haeri Boroujeni, Abolfazl Razi

item.title: Skew-Induced Insertion Loss Deviation (SILD) and FOM_SILD: Metrics for Quantifying P/N Skew Effects in High-Speed Channels
item.description: arXiv:2506.15105v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rise of AI workloads and growing data center demands have driven the need for ultra-high-speed interconnects exceeding 200 Gb/s. As unit intervals (UI) shrink, even a few picoseconds of P/N skew can degrade serializer-deserializer (SerDes) performance. Traditional methods for quantifying skew fall short in capturing its impact. We introduce two new metrics: 1) Skew-Induced Insertion Loss Deviation (SILD) and 2) its complementary Figure of Merit (FOM_SILD), analytically developed to assess P/N skew effects. Measured S-parameters confirm FOM_SILD reciprocity, while simulations of 224G PAM4 SerDes show strong correlation with bit error rate (BER) trends. This approach offers a robust framework for analyzing skew in next-generation ultra-high-speed interconnects.
item.dc:creator: David Nozadze, Zurab Kiguradze, Amendra Koul, Mike Sapozhnikov

item.title: Calibrated uncertainty quantification for prosumer flexibility aggregation in ancillary service markets
item.description: arXiv:2601.14663v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reliable forecasting of prosumer flexibility is critical for demand response aggregators in frequency controlled ancillary service markets, where reliability requirements such as the P90 standard are enforced. Limited behavioural data and dependence on exogenous forecasts introduce uncertainty into flexibility estimates, which can cause reserve overestimation and financial penalties. This study systematically evaluates established uncertainty quantification approaches based on Monte Carlo dropout (MCD), conformal prediction (CP), and conformalised quantile regression (CQR) to construct prediction intervals for aggregated prosumer flexibility and support uncertainty-aware bidding. The approaches are evaluated for a behind-the-meter aggregator in the Danish manual frequency restoration reserve capacity market, using a large-scale synthetic dataset generated with an industry-grade home energy management system and publicly available load, solar, price, activation, and device-level data. Multiple multivariate CP strategies are applied to MCD predictions, alongside CQR using a separately trained quantile regression model. Under nominal test conditions, conformal methods substantially improve joint coverage over uncalibrated MCD baselines. More conservative methods satisfy the 90% lower-tail reliability requirement, while CQR and multivariate CP (MCP) yield narrower intervals and higher economic value, retaining approximately 69% and 68% of perfect-information profit, respectively, under the stricter penalty interpretation. A controlled robustness analysis shows that increasing perturbations of load, solar, price, and activation inputs increase overbidding and reduce coverage and economic performance. The results highlight the trade-off between reliability, economic value, and robustness to input uncertainty in aggregator bidding.
item.dc:creator: Yogesh Pipada Sunil Kumar, S. Ali Pourmousavi, Jon A. R. Liisberg, Julian Lemos-Vinasco

item.title: Network-Aware Progressive Replacement Sequence Planning for Laser-Enhanced BeiDou Navigation Constellations
item.description: arXiv:2607.25235v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The early satellites of the third-generation BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS-3) are approaching the end of their design lifetime, making progressive constellation replacement an inevitable engineering task. Meanwhile, laser inter-satellite links (LISLs) offer high-precision time transfer, ranging, and high-rate data forwarding, providing a promising upgrade path for future BeiDou satellites. This paper investigates the replacement-sequence planning problem for progressively replacing legacy microwave satellites with laser-enabled satellites from a networking perspective. Since practical replacement decisions remain constrained by legacy satellite lifetime, on-orbit condition, laser satellite manufacturing readiness, and launch scheduling, networking information is used as an auxiliary criterion in the actual engineering replacement process. An integer linear programming model is developed to evaluate the network value of intermediate laser--microwave hybrid states. Based on this common state evaluator, two complementary planning methods are developed. A priority-aware exact method supports round-wise network-assisted launch decisions, while a visibility-guided adaptive large-neighborhood search is used for full-sequence planning and provides a full-horizon network-oriented near-optimal reference. Simulations using the actual BDS-3 constellation show that stronger network participation leads to earlier and larger ground-connected laser subnetworks, fewer microwave-dependent satellites, better coordination between laser-backbone growth and high-rate ground access, and improved residual microwave-layer performance. These results provide a quantitative basis for incorporating network performance as an auxiliary criterion in future BeiDou replacement planning.
item.dc:creator: Huan Yan, Juan A. Fraire, Ziqi Yang, Kanglian Zhao, Wenfeng Li, Jinjun Zheng, Ziyu Wang, Changgang Zheng

item.title: Physically Constrained Agentic AI for Energy Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2608.09029v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agentic AI extends energy management beyond fixed-form interaction by translating natural-language requests into coordinated scheduling actions. We present a hierarchical ReAct Energy Management System (EMS) in which one orchestrator coordinates specialist agent types for shiftable appliances, EV charging, and thermal control. Physical authorization is separated from language generation: a deterministic critic reconstructs each integrated day-ahead candidate and checks its schema, appliance cycles, device power, thermal comfort, and, when active, the whole power feeder limit. Across Qwen 3.5 checkpoints, single-appliance mixed-integer schedules were feasible in 83.3 percent of runs. Localized feedback produced no accepted coupled schedule, whereas a multi-step policy authorized 6/6 current coupled runs: 3/3 for 27B and 3/3 for 35B-A3B. The standard occupied-window policy permits pre-conditioning, enforces comfort from 09:00-18:00. Every accepted schedule passed an independent final replay. Feasible costs were 2522.499 JPY for 27B and 1592.697 JPY for 35B-A3B, which are slightly higher than the mathematical optimization optimum of 1343.380 JPY. These results establish a fail-closed workflow for agentic MIP and MILP energy scheduling under the declared physical model.
item.dc:creator: Dafang Zhao, Yang Deng, Zhengmao Li, Zekun Guo, Ka Tai Lau, Samson Tai

item.title: Lightweight Onboard Routing and Topology Co-Construction for Autonomous GNSSs
item.description: arXiv:2609.07056v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Global navigation satellite systems (GNSSs) can already plan their inter-satellite link (ISL) topology onboard, leaving routing as the last step toward autonomous networking. In GNSS ISLs, each satellite links to at most one peer per time slot. We exploit this structure to replace end-to-end path search with a single backward sweep over the slots. The proposed method, DS-SMFP, propagates earliest-arrival times backward from each destination and outputs a STORE/FORWARD decision for every slot, satellite, and destination, in time linear in the number of slots and with working memory independent of the planning horizon. Because each slot needs only its own topology and the delivery state of the next one, routing can steer link selection while the topology is built. This slotwise dependency enables Master-Oriented Topology--Routing Co-Construction (MTRCC), which favors traffic to and from a master satellite performing onboard orbit determination. In a 24-h, 30-satellite BeiDou scenario, DS-SMFP matches the delays of Contact Graph Routing (CGR) and shortest path tree (SPT) routing while running over 180 times faster and using over 36 times less peak routing working memory. Compared with fair contact plan (FCP) topology, MTRCC reduces mean master-related traffic delays by over 10\%, with an approximately 3\% increase in mean PDOP. This paper provides a methodological foundation for efficient autonomous GNSS networking.
item.dc:creator: Huan Yan, Juan A. Fraire, Rongqin Yang, Wenfeng Li, Kanglian Zhao

item.title: Dissipation Bounds and Hardness in Globally Asymptotically Stable Quadratic Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.29512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Approximating the maximum retained energy fraction in globally asymptotically stable quadratic systems of growing dimension is NP-hard at every fixed positive additive error below $1/2$, even when strict quartic Lyapunov functions and strictness proofs are constructed in polynomial time and included in the input. Polynomial-factor approximation is also NP-hard for the least dissipated fraction, energy-halving time and structured coefficient distance to loss of asymptotic stability. For a partially damped family, minimum unit-sphere coupling norm equals that distance, with two-sided inverse-square halving-time bounds at distances in $(0,1/2]$ and explicit coefficient factors. Additive hardness persists under structured coefficient perturbations and direct damping, even with global exponential stability, a strict quadratic Lyapunov function and a Hurwitz Jacobian.
item.dc:creator: Subhransu S. Bhattacharjee

item.title: Evolutionary Deep Nets for Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
item.description: arXiv:2303.03538v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Compact appliance classifiers can support local electricity-load monitoring where memory and computation are constrained. We evaluate adaptive sparse evolutionary training and warm-start compression using synthetic aggregate windows derived from household appliance recordings. A completed convolutional network study trains 120 models over four targets and three seeds with validation-only model selection. Two analyses examine compression with approximately preserved binary accuracy and joint improvement in positive-class F1 and sparsity. Relative to a newly trained fixed sparse evolutionary baseline, the selected compressed policy changes accuracy from 91.53%, while increasing macro F1 to 92.40%. Stored weights decrease by 17.36% and active first-layer connections by 23.93%. Refinement requires additional training. Three seeds and unverified source-window independence prevent claims of statistical equivalence or unseen-house performance.
item.dc:creator: Jinsong Wang, Kenneth A. Loparo

item.title: On the Gradient Domination of the LQG Problem
item.description: arXiv:2507.09026v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider solutions to the linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) regulator problem via policy gradient (PG) methods. Although PG methods have demonstrated strong theoretical guarantees in solving the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem, despite its nonconvex landscape, their theoretical understanding in the LQG setting remains limited. Notably, the LQG problem lacks gradient dominance in the classical parameterization, i.e., with a dynamic controller, which hinders global convergence guarantees. In this work, we study a PG method for the LQG problem by adopting an alternative parameterization of the set of stabilizing controllers and employing a lifting argument. We refer to this parameterization as a history representation of the control input as it is parameterized by past input and output data from the previous p time-steps. Under this parameterization, the infinite-history LQG optimization reduces to an equivalent static state-feedback LQR problem, allowing us to recover gradient dominance and smoothness. For finite history length p, we establish model-based and model-free convergence guarantees up to a geometrically decaying history-truncation error.
item.dc:creator: Kasra Fallah, Leonardo F. Toso, James Anderson

item.title: Initialization-Free LEO Doppler Positioning via Semidefinite Relaxation: A Cold-Start Approach
item.description: arXiv:2509.17198v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite Doppler measurements offer an alternative source of positioning information for Internet of Things devices when Global Navigation Satellite System signals are unavailable. Conventional local optimisation methods depend on an accurate initial position and can fail during a complete cold start. We propose an initialization-free LEO Doppler positioning framework based on semidefinite relaxation. The method reformulates the nonlinear positioning problem into a semidefinite programme to obtain a receiver position estimate without prior location knowledge. We analyse relaxation tightness under noiseless conditions and derive sufficient noise bounds under parameter disturbances. Simulations and field experiments using opportunistic Iridium-NEXT signals evaluate initialization sensitivity, positioning accuracy and computational cost. In the field experiment, the proposed method achieves a three-dimensional positioning error of 140 m without an initial position, whereas local solvers converge to poor solutions under large initial offsets. Using the semidefinite estimate to initialise Gauss-Newton or Dog-Leg reduces the positioning error to 130 m. The framework provides a cold-start initialization stage for subsequent local refinement in opportunistic LEO positioning. The implementation and datasets are publicly available to support reproducibility and further research.
item.dc:creator: Baoshan Song, Weisong Wen, Qi Zhang, Bing Xu, Penggao Yan, Yuan Li, Li-Ta Hsu

item.title: Bayesian Ambiguity Contraction-based Adaptive Robust Markov Decision Processes for Adversarial Surveillance Missions
item.description: arXiv:2512.01660v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCAs) are envisioned to enable autonomous Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) missions in contested environments, where adversaries may act strategically to deceive or evade detection. These missions pose challenges due to model uncertainty and the need for safe, real-time decision-making. Robust Markov Decision Processes (RMDPs) provide worst-case guarantees but are limited by static ambiguity sets that capture initial uncertainty without adapting to new observations. This paper presents an adaptive RMDP framework tailored to ISR missions with CCAs. We introduce a mission-specific formulation in which the CCA alternates between movement and sensing states. Adversarial uncertainty is represented by finite threat prototypes defining observation, exposure, and state-action transition models. Our approach incrementally refines policies by eliminating inconsistent threat models, allowing the CCA to move from worst-case protection toward more efficient mission policies while maintaining robustness. We establish fixed point stability, agreement with nominal planning as credible sets identify the true node-specific threat prototypes, and a conservative expected value guarantee while those prototypes remain credible. Experiments under Gaussian and non-Gaussian threat models across diverse network topologies show higher mission rewards and fewer exposure events compared to nominal and static robust planners.
